newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends down, gasoline up on stock data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends down, gasoline up on stock data.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil ended lower Wednesday as warmer weather and high production caused a bearish build in supplies, while gasoline prices gained after weekly oil inventory data showed a bullish draw in stocks.
"There was a huge amount of selling of heat for gasoline," said a trader.
November heating oil ended off 1.37 cents to 68.46 cents a gallon a day before its expiry Thursday.
Heat has lost its backwardation with stocks rebuilding to adequate levels, though traders said nearby intermonth spreads are still too tight to encourage delivery for storage.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday evening that total distillate stocks, which include heating oil and diesel, grew 3.6 million barrels for the week ended October 25 after being at historical lows.

Heating oil stocks gained 1.6 million barrels with distillate production at a record 3.8 million barrels a day. Dealers said output had outstripped demand due to warmer weather in the key northeast U.S. market.
Meanwhile, November gasoline ended up 0.90 cents a gallon at 70.00 cents, while December crude ended off six cents at $24.28 a barrel.
Traders said crude was mostly rangebound Wednesday, pulled in both directions by gasoline and heat.
"(Technically) this close is constructive for gasoline," said Jake Bernstein, president of MBH Commodity Advisors in Northbrook, Illinois.
Gasoline is trading at six month highs and does not face major resistance until 78.10, it's post-Gulf War high set in April, traders said.
Behind gasoline's strength is tightening supplies due to refiners focussing on distillate production at the expense of gasoline.
The API said gasoline stocks dropped 3.8 million barrels in the latest week. November gasoline expires Thursday.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
